study type: Retrospective population-based cohort study for prediction model development and validation
exposure: obstetric information from the first birth (including prior sphincter injury)
cohort: The study included 609,916 women with first or second deliveries of singleton pregnancies, cephalic presentations, and gestational age >=37 + 0 weeks, occurring in Sweden between 2009 and 2017.
finding: Fetal birth weight was identified as the crucial predictor of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI), with obstetric interventions, particularly vacuum delivery, also being significant contributors to the risk.
mod_finding: Vacuum delivery significantly predicted OASI, contributing 33% and 29% of the predictive information (R2(N)) in first and second vaginal deliveries, respectively.
birth_weight: Birth weight was identified as the primary predictor of OASI, contributing 31%-45% of the predictive information in the full models.
